Lo que hoy sabemos sobre la cena: lo ideal es cenar lo más temprano posible, para que el cuerpo haga una digestión adecuada antes de dormir, evitar el reflujo, no sentirte pesado y descansar mejor. La cena tampoco debería ser la comida más abundante del día, sobre todo en proteína: la #proteína se aprovecha mejor repartida de forma uniforme entre desayuno, almuerzo y cena. Para calcularla, el Dr. Jaramillo explica la fórmula de 1,5 gramos de proteína por kilo de peso al día, con ejemplos de cómo distribuirla. Además, la cena necesita buena cantidad de fibra (alrededor de 30 gramos al día) y grasas saludables como huevo, aguacate, aceite de oliva, semillas y la grasa de las carnes. También aclara que no necesitas comer cada dos horas después de cenar para "mantener el metabolismo activo".

outliers.descripcion:
Michael Davidson is a world-renowned cardiologist, lipidologist, and the founding CEO of NewAmsterdam Pharma. He begins this episode by sharing how his family history shaped his interest in lipidology and primary prevention. He explains why prevention should focus on causal drivers of disease rather than near-term risk and examines the causal relationship between LDL and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

0:00:00 - Intro
0:00:11 - Michael’s path to lipidology, and his passion for primary prevention
0:07:54 - Reframing prevention around causal drivers rather than time horizon
0:14:11 - What CETP inhibition does, the evolutionary biology of CETP, the HDL-raising rationale, and Pfizer's torcetrapib failure
0:24:38 - Why raising HDL is thought to be beneficial, a quick review of the functions of HDL, and how this connects to torcetrapib
0:28:29 - The graveyard of CETP inhibitors: Roche's dalcetrapib, Lilly's evacetrapib, and Merck's REVEAL trial
0:37:13 - The causality of LDL in cardiovascular disease
0:40:23 - Reviving obicetrapib at NewAmsterdam, and confirming the benefit is LDL lowering: the TULIP data, the abandoned statin-intolerance path, and the Mendelian randomization verdict on HDL
0:49:21 - Phase 2 and phase 3 trials of obicetrapib—ROSE, BROOKLYN, BROADWAY, and TANDEM—and the PREVAIL outcomes trial, with the European and US approval paths
0:56:07 - Discordance among LDL-C, LDL-P, and apoB with CETP inhibition, and obicetrapib's Lp(a)-lowering effect
